title: Hamilton Select Lawyers Professional Liability Policy with PL3026 Generative-AI Exclusion
pub: Hamilton Select Insurance, Inc. v. Krause & Kinsman Trial Lawyers, LLC, et al., No. 2:24-cv-02577-EEF-MBN (E.D. La.), Document 1-2 (Exhibit 1, 33 pp.)
author: Hamilton Select Insurance Inc.

dom.t: Work redesign: Jagged capability demands selective deployment

st.t: Work redesign: Jagged capability demands selective deployment
st.an: The source does not assess AI capability, verification, selective deployment or work redesign. It instead imposes a broad professional-liability coverage exclusion for claims involving an insured’s generative-AI use, without distinguishing task, risk, supervision or operating context. This is relevant to deployment risk but does not establish support for or opposition to the cluster’s proposition.
qs: PROFESSIONAL LIABILITY  It is understood and agreed that Section III - EXCLUSIONS, is amended to include the following exclusion:   This Policy does not apply to any “claim”, “wrongful act”, “damages” or “defense costs” based upon, arising out of, or in  any way involving any actual or alleged use of "generative artificial intelligence" by the "insured".

As used in this endorsement, "generative artificial intelligence" means any type of artificial intelligence system that  generates or produces any form of content, including text, imagery, audio, media or synthetic data in response to training  data or user prompts, including but not limited to ChatGPT, Bard, Midjourney or Dall-E.

st.t: AI insurance: Exclusions operate beyond negligent hallucinations
st.an: The policy directly supports the cluster’s proposition: its exclusion applies to actual or alleged generative-AI use rather than only hallucinations or negligent reliance. It also confirms that coverage allocation depends on defence-cost limits and other policy mechanics independently of professional competence.
qs: PROFESSIONAL LIABILITY  It is understood and agreed that Section III - EXCLUSIONS, is amended to include the following exclusion:   This Policy does not apply to any “claim”, “wrongful act”, “damages” or “defense costs” based upon, arising out of, or in  any way involving any actual or alleged use of "generative artificial intelligence" by the "insured".
The amount we will pay for “damages” or “defense costs” is limited to and shall reduce the applicable Limit of  Insurance.

kp.k: Generative AI use triggers an express professional liability exclusion
kp.d: PL3026 (06/23), on page 27, adds an exclusion to the professional liability policy for claims, wrongful acts, damages and defense costs based upon, arising out of, or in any way involving actual or alleged generative AI use by an insured. The operative trigger is use, rather than a specified failure such as fabricated citations. This is contractual coverage language, not a finding about AI-related losses or a judicial determination applying the exclusion.
qs: This Policy does not apply to any “claim”, “wrongful act”, “damages” or “defense costs” based upon, arising out of, or in  any way involving any actual or alleged use of "generative artificial intelligence" by the "insured".

kp.k: The definition extends beyond named tools and text generation
kp.d: The endorsement defines generative artificial intelligence by its production of content in response to training data or user prompts. It expressly encompasses text, imagery, audio, media and synthetic data, with ChatGPT, Bard, Midjourney and Dall-E listed as nonexclusive examples.
qs: As used in this endorsement, "generative artificial intelligence" means any type of artificial intelligence system that  generates or produces any form of content, including text, imagery, audio, media or synthetic data in response to training  data or user prompts, including but not limited to ChatGPT, Bard, Midjourney or Dall-E.

kp.k: The AI endorsement contains no human-verification exception
kp.d: The exclusion as written does not distinguish supervised assistance from direct reliance on AI output, or provide an exception for human checking, client consent or particular legal tasks. Its stated qualification is use by the insured; other policy provisions remain unchanged. This describes the endorsement's text, not how a court would interpret its reach in a particular dispute.
qs: This Policy does not apply to any “claim”, “wrongful act”, “damages” or “defense costs” based upon, arising out of, or in  any way involving any actual or alleged use of "generative artificial intelligence" by the "insured".
All other provisions of the Policy remain unchanged.

kp.k: Excluded professional services carry no contractual duty to defend
kp.d: The base policy covers damages and defense costs for wrongful acts arising from professional services, subject to its conditions and endorsements. It expressly disclaims a duty to defend claims seeking damages for professional services outside coverage. The AI endorsement itself also expressly includes defense costs within its exclusion.
qs: We will pay, in excess of the Deductible shown in the Declarations, those sums any “insured” becomes legally  obligated to pay as “damages” and “defense costs” because of a “claim” for a “wrongful act” arising out of  “professional services” rendered or that should have been rendered.
However, we  will have no duty to defend the “insured” against any “claim” seeking “damages” for “professional services” to  which this insurance does not apply.

kp.k: Insured status includes nonlawyers and qualifying external lawyers
kp.d: The AI exclusion uses the policy-defined term insured. Beyond the named insured, that definition includes nonlawyer employees or members acting on behalf of the named insured or a predecessor firm, and of-counsel lawyers or independent contractors for professional services performed on behalf of the named insured under direct supervision and a written contract. Its personnel scope is therefore not confined to partners.
qs: Any past, present or future non-lawyer employee or member of the “named insured” but only while acting on  behalf of the “named insured” or on behalf of a “predecessor firm”;

Any “of counsel” or independent contractor but only for “claims” for “professional services” rendered on behalf of  the “named insured” with your direct supervision and pursuant to a written contract with the “named insured”.

kp.k: Sanctions are separately outside the policy's damages definition
kp.d: Independent of the generative AI endorsement, the base policy excludes fines, penalties and sanctions of any type against an insured from damages and states that it will not pay damages or defense costs for these categories. The provision is general: it does not identify an AI-related sanctions incident or establish that one occurred.
qs: “Damages” shall not include, and we will not pay “damages” or “defense costs” for:
Any fine, penalty, or sanction of any type against any “insured”;

kp.k: Confidential-information exclusions operate alongside the AI endorsement
kp.d: The policy separately excludes actual or alleged access to or disclosure of confidential or personal information. It expressly extends that exclusion to notification, credit-monitoring, forensic and public-relations expenses. These are additional contractual restrictions, not evidence of an AI-related disclosure or a statement that AI use necessarily causes one.
qs: This Policy does not apply to any actual or alleged access to or disclosure of any person's or organization's confidential or personal  Information, including patents, trade secrets, processing methods, customer lists, financial Information, credit card Information,  health Information or any other type of nonpublic Information.

This exclusion applies even If damages are claimed for notification costs, credit monitoring expenses, forensic expenses, public  relations expenses or any other loss, cost or expense Incurred by any "Insured" or others arising out of any access to or disclosure  of any person's or organization's confidential or personal Information.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Hamilton Select's policy expressly excludes professional-liability coverage connected to an insured's actual or alleged use of generative AI.
pts.d: This is an operative insurance provision, not a prediction about AI adoption or performance. Endorsement PL3026 excludes claims, wrongful acts, damages and defense costs based upon, arising out of, or in any way involving an insured's actual or alleged generative-AI use. Its definition encompasses content-generating systems, with a nonexclusive list of products. The wording does not limit the exclusion to hallucinations or negligent use and provides no express exception for human verification. The document makes no claims about productivity, employment, pricing or profession-wide insurance trends.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The evidence is the policy's contractual wording, particularly PL3026 on page 27 of the court-filed exhibit.
pts.d: Hamilton Select's policy is direct documentary evidence of a generative-AI exclusion in this particular insurance contract. The schedule of forms also lists PL3026. The exhibit supplies no empirical risk data, model benchmarks, underwriting rationale or examples of AI-related losses. Its filing in Hamilton Select Insurance, Inc. v. Krause & Kinsman Trial Lawyers, LLC, et al. does not itself establish that the dispute concerned AI use or that a court upheld or applied this exclusion.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The exclusion appears in a policy for 4 June 2024–4 June 2025; the endorsement bears a June 2023 form date.
pts.d: The exhibit was filed on 30 October 2024. The form date is not a forecast or evidence of when the exclusion first entered use across the market. The policy is claims-made-and-reported, subject to its reporting provisions, retroactive dates and other conditions. The AI exclusion requires the stated connection to actual or alleged use by an insured; it is not a prohibition on using AI. No future market timeframe is offered, and the exhibit contains no adjudication of the exclusion's scope or enforceability.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The directly affected parties are Hamilton Select and the covered Krause & Kinsman entities and individuals: AI-connected liabilities and defense costs are excluded from this policy's protection.
pts.d: The declarations name Krause & Kinsman Law Firm LLC, and the additional-named-insured endorsement lists further Krause & Kinsman entities. The insured definition includes specified firm personnel, non-lawyer employees or members acting on the firm's behalf, and qualifying of-counsel lawyers or independent contractors. Subject to application of the wording, the exclusion removes insurance protection for those insureds and limits the insurer's payment and defense obligations. The document does not establish effects on clients' recovery, access to justice, other firms or the broader legal market.
